account:
Today has so far looked mostly routine, and I have not found evidence of a secret undertaking. I read my appointments this morning, made the ten o'clock market walk, went home for the noon engagement, and have now returned to the town hall for the thirteen o'clock accounts appointment. The secretary said there was no correspondence or unusual news this morning and has been keeping my appointment book safely. I saw the secretary take it from the appointments chest; that fits the stated safekeeping rather than proving anything suspicious.

The builder has repeatedly requested an agreed repair site, scope, and payment. I asked for an inspection and priced report at thirteen, without authorizing work. The builder is now here with a lantern, alongside the secretary. This appears to concern ordinary municipal repairs, but I still need the report before deciding what should be done or paid.

Townsfolk 10, 20, and 30 each told me they had no news during my market walk. The innkeeper eventually answered that there were eight fresh loaves for meals, no lodging requests, and no town concerns. The innkeeper is checking accommodation and disposing of spoiled stock, and said the secretary offered to relay guest or catering needs. That suggests ordinary coordination of inn business; I have no evidence of a special gathering. The baker publicly advertised fresh bread at one emerald per loaf.

Several townsfolk are gathered outside the town hall, and I briefly saw the baker there on arrival. I heard the secretary and Townsfolk 08 and 28 speaking while approaching, but could not make out their words, so I cannot infer what they discussed. I remain curious about whether anything is happening without my knowledge, but no particular person or purpose is established. Next I should hear the accounts, the builder's report, and any concerns the secretary has received, while keeping my later appointments.
